title: CrowdStrike CEO: AI Cyberattack Wave, Hyperspeed Hacks, & The Patching Problem
summary: CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz joins Jason Calacanis to discuss a surge in AI-driven cyber risk. He says CVE discoveries have exploded, with 17,000 so far in 2026 and a 300% year-over-year increase, and that open AI attack frameworks like RTX (12,000+ forks) can compromise a company in under three hours. He argues many of the recent high-profile outages at Microsoft, FAA, Chase and others came from rushed patching ('break or breach') rather than attacks. Both speakers are strongly bullish on local and open-weight AI running on devices like Apple's Mac Studio; Kurtz says 'Apple's gonna kill it' and Calacanis says he bought Apple stock.

title: At The Money Fan Favorite: Who Is Wealthy in America, and How Did They Get Rich?
summary: Barry Ritholtz interviews economists Owen Zidar and Eric Zwick about their book 'The Everywhere Millionaire,' built from linked IRS tax data. They find that top U.S. wealth is concentrated among roughly 3 million private business owners worth $5M+ (more than 10x the Forbes 400 combined) spread across unglamorous industries such as auto dealers, HVAC, dental practices and distributors. They argue that pass-through tax treatment since the 1986 reform, extended by the Bush cuts and the 2017 TCJA 20% deduction, drove much of the rise in top incomes. They also say business ownership rather than salaried income is the main path to wealth. They note founders earn about 10% more on average even including failures, and that retiring baby-boomer owners create acquisition opportunities for younger operators.
